commands.review_summary:
The PR adds `useUtilityModel: true` to Crestodian approval-intent model preparation and adds a regression test asserting that option is passed.

PR surface: Source +4, Tests +11. Total +15 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection shows an ambiguous approval reply reaches `classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent`, whose current-main model-preparation call omits the selector flag that chooses `utilityModel`; I did not run a live provider completion in this read-only review.

target.title: fix(crestodian): run approval-intent classifier on the utilityModel, not flagship (#102360)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Crestodian approval-intent classifier (`classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent`, `src/crestodian/approval-intent.ts`) resolves the completion model **without** `useUtilityModel: true`, so an ambiguous approval reply that reaches the model path runs on the agent's **flagship** model to decide a single approve/decline/other label. It was the only member of the simple-completion family (e.g. `conversation-label-generator.ts`) that omitted the flag, so every ambiguous approval reply is billed at flagship pricing for a fixed ~8-token structured answer. Fixes #102360.

## Why This Change Was Made

A one-word bounded classification is exactly the "utility work" the rest of the family already runs on the configured `utilityModel`. `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` already supports `useUtilityModel` (resolves `agents.defaults.utilityModel`); the classifier just wasn't passing it. Adding `useUtilityModel: true` aligns it with the family and the cheaper tier.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a distinct `utilityModel` (the intended cheap tier for bounded classification) stop paying flagship pricing for ambiguous approval-flow replies. No behavior change to the classification result — only the model tier that judges it.

## Evidence

Real `classifyCrestodianApprovalIntent` call with an ambiguous message (model path), capturing what model prep receives:
```
before (main):    prepare called with useUtilityModel = undefined   ← flagship
after  (this PR): prepare called with useUtilityModel = true        ← utilityModel
```
Added a regression test asserting `prepareSimpleCompletionModelForAgent` is called with `{ useUtilityModel: true }`. `tsgo:core` 0 errors; `approval-intent.test.ts` green (8 tests: 7 existing + 1 new).
